summary: GKE service-account annotations failing to normalize -> IAM binding drift in prod env
description: Several prod namespaces created by the onboarding pipeline lost expected IAM rolebindings after a recent rollout of the annotation-normalizer. Customers running private deployments observed jobs failing with 403 when the platform attempted to access GCS/Secrets. Early signs point to annotation key truncation in the normalizer which prevents the iam-syncer from mapping ServiceAccount annotations -> cloud IAM bindings for the environment. Impact: intermittent tenant job failures and elevated support noise. Scope: a subset of namespaces created between 2026-03-11 22:00 UTC and 2026-03-12 04:30 UTC in gke-us-east-cluster-a.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create namespace via onboarding pipeline with serviceaccount annotations: redwood.dev/role=env-prod-data-access and redwood.dev/env=prod-us-east
2) Observe annotation-normalizer webhook call and resulting formatted annotations on the ServiceAccount resource
3) Check iam-syncer logs to see mapping attempt for annotation key; expect binding creation for service account to cloud IAM role
4) Confirm binding missing in cloud console and application 403 on accessing protected resource
logs: normalizer: INFO 2026-03-12T00:03:11Z received annotations for svcacct: annotations length OK
normalizer: WARN 2026-03-12T00:03:11Z truncated annotation key redwood.dev/role -> redwood.dev/rol
iam-syncer: ERROR 2026-03-12T00:03:12Z no mapping found for annotation key redwood.dev/rol, skipping binding for svcacct: onboarding-prod-123
comments: Priya Malhotra (Reporter) 2026-03-12: Noticed multiple tenant onboarding failures; filing internal ticket and tagging SRE/Platform. Started temporary mitigation by re-annotating one affected SA manually.

Ethan Cole (Assignee) 2026-03-12: Investigating normalizer change deployed in release 'ops-config@release-2026-03-11'. Suspect a string width enforcement introduced in PR ops-config#1423. Will try rollback in staging first.
SRE Team 2026-03-12: Confirmed prod spike of IAM sync errors at 00:03-04:30 UTC correlated with release window. Placing rate-limited retry on iam-syncer to reduce churn while root cause investigated.
Security 2026-03-12: Flagging that manual reannotation creates transient elevated-permission steps; recommend scoped service to perform correction instead of broad role grants.
investigation_notes: Reproduced locally: normalizer enforces annotation key length <= 16 chars and truncates suffix, introduced by validator in ops-config#1423

Observed mismatch: annotation expected 'redwood.dev/role' (16 chars after slash) but normalizer truncated to 'redwood.dev/rol' on keys that happened to exceed internal limit when combined with prefixes
iam-syncer lookup uses exact annotation key matching; no canonicalization for truncated keys -> mapping miss
Audit of change history: ops-config deploy at 2026-03-11T22:48:11Z included a new normalization library upstream, tests covered values but not key-length behavior
Temporary mitigation attempted: roll back ops-config to previous stable tag on one canary cluster -> restores bindings for new namespaces created after rollback
Confirmed that pre-existing namespaces (created before deploy) are unaffected because they retained original keys; the issue impacts new creations only
Risk assessment: low blast radius if rollback proceeds but need migration for the ~120 namespaces created in the 6.5hr window
resolution_summary: Rolled back annotation-normalizer change from ops-config@release-2026-03-11 across all control-plane webhooks for GKE in us-east. Created a remediation job to re-annotate affected ServiceAccounts and trigger iam-syncer rebinds. IAM bindings restored for all validated namespaces.
resolution_notes: 2026-03-12 02:15 UTC: Rolled back ops-config release on gke-us-east-cluster-a via canary -> full rollback. Monitoring shows iam-syncer errors dropped to baseline by 02:30 UTC.

2026-03-12 06:10 UTC: Ran remediation job (scripts/iam-fixup) that reads backups, computes expected annotation keys, applies correct annotations, and forces iam-syncer reconciliation for 128 affected namespaces.
PR to ops-config: github.com/redwood-inference/ops-config/pull/1431 created to remove key-length truncation and add targeted unit tests for annotation keys
Added monitoring alert 'iam-syncer.annotation-mismatch' to trigger at >5 errors/min sustained for 5m
Notified CS and Platform leads; customer-facing impact limited and most tenants auto-recovered once bindings were re-applied
follow_up_tasks: INT-424681: Add annotation key canonicalization to iam-syncer to tolerate minor formatting differences and log mapping misses
INT-424682: Add unit and integration tests in ops-config to prevent truncation regressions for annotation keys and values
INT-424683: Run audit script to list annotation patterns in all clusters and surface any nonconforming keys
Update onboarding runbook: include steps to re-run iam-syncer reconciliation job and safe rollback playbook
notes_for_release_review: Root cause was a misguided normalization change applied without test coverage for annotation key format. The fix removes enforced truncation and adds explicit tests. Recommend expanding canary windows for control-plane webhooks and adding a schema contract between normalizer and iam-syncer.
